lessons.title: Chain Rule and Compound Proportion
lessons.concept: Chain rule in aptitude extends direct and inverse proportion to situations involving more than two quantities. To find an unknown, compare each quantity with the quantity of interest and determine whether the relationship is direct or inverse, then multiply factors accordingly.
lessons.formula: M1*D1*H1/W1 = M2*D2*H2/W2 for work problems (men, days, hours, work) when efficiency constant; adjust for direct/inverse relations as needed.
lessons.worked_example: If 5 workers do a job in 12 days, 10 workers (double, direct inverse with days for same work) take 6 days. If also work doubles, days double again to 12.
mistakes: Not identifying which quantity is held constant conceptually
Arithmetic errors when combining multiple ratios
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Applying Direct and Inverse Relations
lessons.concept: A relation is direct if increasing one increases the other (e.g., more work -> more days at same rate). It is inverse if increasing one decreases the other (e.g., more workers -> fewer days for same work). Set up the equation by writing the ratio of the target quantity and multiplying by ratios of other quantities (>1 or <1) based on effect.
lessons.formula: x2 = x1 * (factor1) * (factor2) ..., where factor > 1 if change increases x, factor < 1 if change decreases x (for direct/inverse accordingly).
lessons.worked_example: 10 men build a wall in 8 days. How many days for 16 men? More men -> fewer days (inverse): days = 8 * (10/16) = 5 days.
mistakes: Using 16/10 instead of 10/16 for inverse relation
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Multi-step Chain Rule Problems
lessons.concept: Complex problems involve several variables (men, days, hours/day, efficiency, work amount). Handle one factor at a time or use the compound formula. Ensure all compared scenarios are consistent in units.
lessons.formula: Work proportional to men*days*hours*efficiency (general form). Keep ratios consistent.
lessons.worked_example: 6 machines produce 120 units in 4 days. Units by 9 machines in 5 days (same rate) = 120 * (9/6) * (5/4) = 120 * 1.5 * 1.25 = 225 units.
mistakes: Forgetting one of the factors (e.g., hours per day)
Applying inverse factor when relation is direct
